analysis.file_name: GS Blekos - ## GOAL Kickstart US Consumer Outlook US Semis DC in Europe RHM Pluxee Indus Heatmap Naturgy ## 10 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart / US Consumer Outlook / US Semis / DC in Europe / RHM / Pluxee / Indus Heatmap / Naturgy
key_insights: GS remains overweight equities over 3m and 12m, citing earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end. It also remains overweight cash because near-term volatility may linger on AI uncertainty and Middle East tensions.

GS sees three paths to a rebound in risk appetite: easing AI concerns with signs of monetisation, rates relief possibly helped by falling energy prices, and a larger decline of its RAI below -1, which improves the asymmetry to add risk into year-end.
GS remains overweight bonds, favouring longer-duration bonds because higher yields and peaking nominal growth give equities a better buffer.

US Economics expects 2027 consumer spending to grow 2.2% (Q4/Q4), near potential. The start of the year is softer on higher rates weighing on durables, elevated energy prices and lower nonprofit spending after the midterms. A pickup follows as inflation pressures abate, tax refunds arrive and the reversal of benefit cuts turns the fiscal impulse modestly positive.

GS sees downside risk to consumer spending from a fading wealth effect. It estimates the effect added over 0.4pp to spending growth in 2026 and about half as much in 2027 in the baseline, and it could weigh on spending if AI-related stocks keep declining.
US semiconductors: GS favours NVDA and AVGO in AI compute, saying they imply no growth from 2027, after a sector-wide pullback.
Semi cap equipment: GS treats 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX.
Memory is approaching oversold levels as GS begins to move toward tangible book value.

European datacenters: GS says the growth path is unaffected by the US midterms. Power generators with power land, connection points and the ability to sign energy supply contracts stand to benefit most.
European power grids are likely to see ongoing capex acceleration, and equipment makers such as Siemens Energy, Vestas and Nordex offer exposure.
Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger took part in a GS fireside chat covering major German programmes, ammunition, naval, air defence, unmanned systems and cash conversion.

GS upgrades Pluxee to Neutral from Sell. The shares are down 31% since the October 14, 2024 Sell List addition, underperforming the STOXX 600 and FTSE World Europe by 55pp, on regulatory headwinds (particularly Brazil) and weaker operating revenue trends that cut consensus earnings.
The note also includes a European multi-industry 3Q26 heatmap and a Naturgy piece on a renewable route to growth.
